title: Subbing with the Oscar Peterson trio in Aspen and the snare drum prank
summary: Shortly before Nat, Lee was whisked to Aspen to replace Irving Ashby with Peterson and Ray Brown, who hid his snare drum as a joke.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong
story.community_name: Pranks, practical jokes and band humor

blocks.x: It was right at the time -- I skipped over this, but before I went with Nat, my son and I were living alone, and Oscar Peterson trio at the time consisted of Irvin Ashby, Ray Brown and Oscar Peterson, so something happened to Ashby and Oscar and Ray had this engagement in Aspen, Colorado, and one evening about 6:30, here they come by my house and they were really a lot of fun.

One guy started taking my drums out to the car, and I said, 'What are you doing?' You know, 'Where you goin'' -- and he said, 'We catch this plane for Denver at 10 o'clock, because something happened to Ashby and you got to go with us.' And I said, 'Well, look, my kid and I live alone; I got to ...' 'We're sorry, we made arrangements; we're gonna take him over to his mother' -- but you know, talking about Bogard ...
Yes, I went. We made the plane by 10 o'clock that night. They come and packed my clothes and took my drums outside and said you can't say no, because I

always said I'm not gonna go anyplace, you know.
So we went up to Aspen, Colorado, and you know,
some of the most enjoyable times that I have ever had in my
life was working with Oscar Peterson. Because he was really
a lot of fun, as well as Ray Brown.

But what they did to me --they believed in practical
jokes. Now we're getting ready to play at this lodge up in
Aspen, Colorado, and I can't find my snare drum. They had
taken my snare drum out of my trap case and hit it from me.
And so I'm setting up the drums and I can't find the snare
drum, and so they keep saying, Ray used to call me "Ripty"
because I used to work with Ray and Hank Jones and Ella,
and he said, "C'mon Ripty, we got to go; we got to hit it."
And I said, "I can't find my snare drum", and so I was really
what they would call up a tree, because I couldn't imagine
how could you leave your snare drum out of your trap case, you
know ...

But I didn't know -- not knowing the practical jokes
they played. And so they started playing -- they opened up
with "Airmail Special" -- and just as fast as you could play
it, and so I had no snare drum, and all of a sudden, here comes
a waiter with a tray, my snare drum on it! Yeah, that was
really a ball I had, you know, playing with them.

Pardon me, but I don't quite follow
why the fact that you worked with Hank Jones and Ella made

them call you "Ripty". Oh, well it was a thing that I always used to say which I guess is not really for the tape -- it was Ripty, gipty, boom ... and so they used to just start calling me Ripty, and I called Ray "Rip" and he calls me "Rip".
I'm gonna let that one alone.
